page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 120 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. The processor is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

This server configuration includes 1745 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across five local drives. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The local NVMe storage provides high-speed local read and write capabilities directly attached to the instance, which supports data-intensive operations without network storage overhead.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in single-threaded tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2304.0 and a gzip compression rate of 36.97 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-threaded performance is also strong, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 52401.15 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 238.42 GB/sec. For database operations, the server achieves 63.56 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, while static web serving throughput reaches 58.17 GB/sec.

The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon processing power, AMX instruction support, and local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance suitable for workloads such as database hosting, web serving, text and image processing, and medium-scale language model inference. The hardware profile offers high resource density and strong benchmark-per-resource tradeoffs for compute-heavy and storage-dependent applications, though memory-bound tasks may be limited by the 3.75 GB per core memory allocation.
